title: Autumn Leaf ABC
hook: Some things change; some green stays with the trees.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
visualStyle: cozy 3D autumn woodland storybook, amber orange and russet leaves, friendly wildlife, strong foreground contrast

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child noticing what changes and what stays the same as one woodland day moves deeper into autumn
creativeFingerprint.chorusFunction: contrast falling color with evergreen continuity
creativeFingerprint.grooveMeter: gentle 3/4 leaf-fall waltz with drifting pickups
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written seasonal observations; color and change are specific, never claim every plant changes the same way
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: season cue -> recall beat -> target -> drift/turn/shape gesture
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. wood-flute or pizzicato leaf answers between target phrases
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: wood-flute or pizzicato leaf answers between target phrases
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Let autumn change the same woodland object by object: some leaves loosen, some plants stay green, damp ground brings mushrooms, animals move through cooler cover, and the forest becomes more open as the canopy thins.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A child watches one autumn day deepen from first falling leaf toward cooler evening; recurring language uses turn, loosen, drift, gather, thin, cool, copper, gold and green-stays-green.
imageMotifs: bare branches revealing nest and knot
semanticArc: cooler damp forest reveals hidden forms
thinning canopy and river carry the season onward
